chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a man who dies leaving behind a slave mother and possessing wealth: 'His mother should be freed by purchasing her from his wealth, and the remainder of the wealth should be given to her, if there is no relative of hers who has a designated share in the Book of Allah.'

key_terms.سَهْمٌ فِي كِتَابِ اللَّهِ: Designated share in the Book of Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling for a slave mother left by her deceased master's estate?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam Ali (AS) establishes the priority of manumitting an 'umm walad' (slave mother of the master's child) from the deceased's estate before distribution to other heirs, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of freeing slaves as a debt of the estate. The condition regarding the absence of other relatives with fixed Quranic shares (dhawu al-furud) highlights the interplay between manumission and the residual inheritance (residuary heirs), ensuring the mother receives the remainder only when no statutory heirs compete for the estate.
